meta.title: Facilities — Production City
meta.description: Explore Production City's planned production facilities: screen sound stages, commercial sound stages, broadcast theatre, broadcast control room, and more.

overview.heading: Planned Facilities
overview.intro: Production City is designed to house a comprehensive portfolio of production facilities, each built to professional broadcast and film specifications.

screenStages.name: Screen Sound Stages
screenStages.description: Large-format sound stages designed for grand-scale productions with configurable LED volume environments.

detail.heading: Grand-scale screen work. Engineered for it.
detail.lead: 2,025 m² of stage floor. 15 m to grid. NRC 1.05. Full-surround LED volume ready.
detail.prose: Feature film. Episodic. Live television. When the production is large-format, the stage has to be built for it from the ground up.
detail.prose2: Each screen sound stage is 45 m × 45 m, 15 m to grid, full-coverage grid and catwalk. Sound-proofing is NRC 1.05 / NC 25. LED volume is configurable flat, arc, or full-surround.
detail.prose3: These stages were designed against the technical specifications of major-studio and streamer productions. As the first site, the standards are set here.

commercialStages.name: Commercial Sound Stages
commercialStages.description: Compact sound stages for commercials, TVCs, music videos, and other smaller-scale content, with configurable LED environments.

detail.heading: Small footprint. Full specification.
detail.lead: 100 m² of stage. Same 15 m to grid. Same sound-proofing. Walk-in-ready LED volume.
detail.prose: Commercials, TVCs, music videos, short-form, and digital work do not need the 45 × 45. They do need proper acoustics, proper height, and the same LED configurations.
detail.prose2: That is what these stages are. Walk in on a Monday. Shoot. Strike by Friday. The volume configurations are shared with the screen stages, so a look developed on one can move to the other.

broadcastTheatre.name: Broadcast Theatre
broadcastTheatre.description: A multi-purpose venue planned for live performance, live broadcast, and immersive theatre experiences with VR/AR compatibility.

detail.heading: A live theatre wired as a broadcast studio.
detail.lead: 450 in theatre mode. 300 in cabaret. Eight fully integrated robotic camera positions. AR and VR ready. Broadcast-partner compliant.
detail.prose: The broadcast theatre is a multi-modal live venue with a broadcast gallery wrapped around it.
detail.prose2: Robotic cameras, an LED virtual set library, and streaming compliance are built into the room. Every performance here can reach the people in the seats and the audience at home at the same time, without a separate broadcast setup.
detail.cta: Discuss a live broadcast or event.

controlRoom.name: Broadcast Control Room
controlRoom.description: Planned central command post for live production coordination, synchronisation, and multi-platform broadcasting.

detail.heading: The nerve centre.
detail.lead: Central production management, live broadcast control, advanced synchronisation — feeding stages, the theatre, and external venues globally.
detail.prose: The control room is the campus’s single broadcast spine. It manages and synchronises every live production on site.
detail.prose2: It is designed to originate broadcast from external sports and event venues anywhere in the world. Production City’s broadcast and data-centre pedigree sits here. The control room is engineered the way critical broadcast infrastructure is engineered.
detail.cap3: Advanced synchronisation across multi-platform and multi-location broadcasts
detail.cap4: Origination from on-campus stages and theatre
detail.cap5: Origination from external sports and event venues globally

ancillary.heading: Ancillary Spaces
ancillary.description: The campus is planned to include supporting spaces and services for complete production operations.

meta.title: Creative & Ecosystem — Production City
meta.description: 17 disciplines. One campus. One operator. From script to delivery — no vendor handoffs.

ecosystem.heading: One campus. One operator.
ecosystem.summary: All 17 disciplines share a campus, a schedule, and a broadcast backbone. They don't coordinate between each other — they're part of the same operation.
ecosystem.principle1: Physical and digital workflows are the same workflow.
ecosystem.principle2: Departments run concurrently. Props and post overlap. Shooting and script development overlap.
ecosystem.principle3: Workshop, stage, and edit suite sit on the same site. No logistics chain.
ecosystem.principle4: Problems get solved in real time because the people who can solve them are in the building.
ecosystem.principle5: One operator means one set of decisions. Less friction for tenants. Cleaner revenue for the company.
ecosystem.benefit2: No handoffs from vendor to vendor.
ecosystem.benefit3: Phases don't stall waiting for the next contractor.
ecosystem.benefit4: Efficiency is structural — it doesn't need to be managed onto it.
ecosystem.benefit5: Cost comes out of logistics, not production quality.
ecosystem.benefit6: Risk sits with us, not the production.

services.stuntRiggingDesc: Stunt coordinators and rigging experts using specialist equipment for complex action.
services.audioMusicDesc: On-set sound recording, sound design, voice-over, music production, and score development.
services.scriptScreenplayDesc: Writers and story developers evolving concepts into scripts and narrative frameworks.
services.graphicDesignDesc: Visuals, branding, posters, and aesthetic consistency across media.
services.animationDesc: 2D/3D animation, motion graphics, and digital frame-by-frame enhancements.
services.postEditingDesc: Editing, colour correction, colour grading, and narrative assembly.
services.modelling3dDesc: 3D artists mapping designs and captures into detailed models, integrating CGI with live footage.
services.motionCaptureDesc: Recording actor movements and facial expressions for application to digital characters.
services.arVrDesc: Immersive audience experiences that blur reality and fiction.
services.broadcastCoordDesc: Scheduling, managing, and executing live broadcasts for real-time coverage.
services.specialEffectsDesc: Mechanical, optical, and visual effects for practical and simulated phenomena.
services.virtualProdDesc: Previsualisation through post-production using advanced digital tools.
services.conceptDevDesc: Visual narratives from ideation through final design.
services.setConstructDesc: Turning blueprints into physical sets with attention to safety and aesthetics.
services.propsDesignDesc: From historically accurate replicas to fantastical objects.
services.costumeDesignDesc: Costumes spanning historical, futuristic, and culture-specific needs.
services.makeupProstheticsDesc: Age progression, creature prosthetics, and character transformation.

caseStudies.heading: How productions use it
caseStudies.disclaimer: Illustrative scenario — not based on actual events
caseStudies.featureFilmDesc: A historical drama shoots across two screen stages with a set built in the workshop next door — props, costume, LED volume, dressing rooms, and post-production on the same campus.
caseStudies.liveBroadcastDesc: A network hosts a large live entertainment show across the main stage and broadcast theatre, with VR/AR on the commercial stages and the control room managing the feed.
caseStudies.modernTheatre: A stage production with a broadcast life
caseStudies.modernTheatreDesc: A theatre company runs nightly performances in the broadcast theatre while the control room sends a simultaneous live stream — the production reaches the room and the screen at the same time.
caseStudies.internationalCollabDesc: Production teams on different campuses shoot concurrently. Schedules, assets, and broadcast origination run across the network under one operator — no separate logistics chain per site.

meta.title: FAQ — Production City
meta.description: Frequently asked questions about Production City's facilities, services, global network, and community engagement.

faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What types of facilities will Production City offer?
faq.a1: Production City plans to offer Screen Sound Stages, Commercial Sound Stages, a Broadcast Control Room, a multi-functional Broadcast Theatre, and spaces for research & development and educational collaborations.
faq.q2: Will Production City's services be available for international locations?
faq.a2: Yes. Production City plans to expand to Singapore, Hawaii, Europe, and mainland USA with consistent facilities and services across all campuses.
faq.q3: What virtual production services will Production City provide?
faq.a3: Production City will offer comprehensive services from pre-production visualization and conceptualisation to post-production editing and effects, plus 3D modelling, CGI, motion capture, and VR/AR.
faq.q4: How will Production City support educational initiatives?
faq.a4: Through planned partnerships with educational institutions, experiential learning opportunities, R&D facilities, and practical skill development programs.
faq.q5: What research and development facilities will Production City include?
faq.a5: A dedicated facility is planned to be embedded in operations to encourage exploration, innovation, and development of future production technologies and storytelling methods.
faq.q6: What kinds of projects will be suitable for Production City?
faq.a6: Feature films, TV series, live telecasts, stage productions, music videos, VR/AR content, and other forms of content creation.
faq.a7: One campus. One operator. The craft and the technology in the same building, under the same management — not coordinated between separate vendors.
faq.q8: What kind of support services will Production City offer for a smooth production process?
faq.a8: End-to-end virtual production, pre-production, filming, post-production, VFX, sound mixing, dressing rooms, catering, on-site set and prop construction, and digitisation services.
faq.q9: What will make Production City's sound stages unique?
faq.a9: Large scale, 15m height to grid, advanced soundproofing, and LED Volume configurations designed for different production needs.
faq.q10: How will Production City's services simplify the production workflow?
faq.a10: By co-locating pre-production, production, and post-production services on one campus to reduce transport, coordination, and scheduling complexity.
faq.q11: What benefits will the LED volume offer for productions?
faq.a11: Flexible configurations, real-time visual effects, efficient background changes, and a cost/time-effective alternative to traditional green screen methods.
faq.q12: How will Production City commit to sustainability efforts?
faq.a12: Through conscious design, energy-efficient systems, waste management, green spaces, and biodiversity-supporting landscaping.
faq.q13: Will the Production City facilities accommodate pre-production and post-production processes?
faq.a13: Yes. Script development, storyboarding, concept design, editing, sound mixing, colour grading, and visual effects will all be part of the planned offering.
faq.q14: How will being a part of the Production City network enrich a creative professional's experience?
faq.a14: Through access to advanced facilities, full production services, a global creative community, workshops, collaborations, and exposure to diverse ideation methods.
faq.q15: Will clients be able to provide their own technical crew, or will Production City supply them?
faq.a15: Both options are planned. Clients will be able to bring their own crew, and Production City will also be able to provide technical support personnel.
faq.q16: How can clients stay updated with the latest developments or offerings at Production City?
faq.a16: By registering interest on the website, subscribing to the newsletter, or following Production City's social media channels.
faq.q17: How will Production City foster talent growth and innovation?
faq.a17: By partnering with educational institutions, offering hands-on learning, maintaining R&D facilities, and running workshops and skill development programs.
faq.q18: What measures will Production City have to ensure safety and security?
faq.a18: Security personnel, surveillance, secure access controls, fire safety systems, and health and safety protocols aligned with industry standards.
faq.q19: How will Production City cater to different scale productions — from independent creators to corporate entities?
faq.a19: By offering facilities planned for all scales of production and the same level of professional support regardless of project size.
faq.q20: What kinds of engagements beyond facility rentals will be possible?
faq.a20: Technology partnerships, education and research collaborations, joint development of filming methods and techniques, and collaborative business models.

services.item13Desc: 2D, 3D, and motion — character and UI work.
services.item14Desc: Asset creation, digital doubles, and set extensions.
services.item16Desc: AR and VR production aligned to the broadcast theatre and volume.
services.item17Desc: Scheduling, orchestration, and delivery of live events.
services.operationalPoint: The point is not the length of this list. The point is that these disciplines share a campus, a schedule, and a broadcast backbone. A prop built in the workshop reaches the stage without a logistics chain. A take finished in the gallery is graded upstairs. A performance recorded on the theatre stage is streamed from the control room in the same hour. This is the operational argument for vertical integration.

meta.title: First Nations approach — Production City
meta.description: Governance, IP and data practice, workforce, community work, and the stories this campus is built to serve are shaped by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of Knowing, Being, and Doing.

firstNations.heading: Embedded, not added on.
firstNations.lead: Our governance, our intellectual property and data practice, our workforce, our community work, and the stories this campus is built to serve are shaped by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of Knowing, Being, and Doing.
firstNations.ackQuote: Production City acknowledges the Traditional Owners of Country throughout Australia, and the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which a Sydney campus would be built. We pay our respects to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Elders past and present. We acknowledge that sovereignty was never ceded, and that storytelling on these lands is among the oldest continuous creative practice anywhere in the world.
firstNations.leadershipBio1: Matthew Compton is Chief Operating Officer and Managing Director. He leads operational delivery across the business. His role in the organisation is a principal reason this approach is implemented rather than spoken about.
firstNations.leadershipBio2: Matthew holds an MBA (Leadership and Enterprise) from the University of Sydney, a Bachelor of Business Management from the University of Queensland, and is a Member of the Australian Institute of Company Directors. He is a sessional academic at the University of Sydney and an Associate Lecturer at Western Sydney University, where he teaches innovation and business leadership and contributes to the WSU Indigenous Centre of Excellence.
firstNations.leadershipBio3: He sits on the University of Sydney Faculty of Medicine and Health First Nations Cultural Safety Advisory Group.
firstNations.ip1: Free, prior, and informed consent is embedded in how we handle material from or referencing First Nations communities.
firstNations.ip2: Provenance is tracked end-to-end. The origin of training data, reference material, captured performance, and derived assets is recorded and auditable.
firstNations.ip3: Cultural safety protocols are built into production workflows, including virtual production, motion capture, and generative tools.
firstNations.ip4: Benefit remains with the people a story comes from — agreements keep recognition and benefit with communities, not the production company by default.
firstNations.onCountryHeading: Education, skills, and community — delivered on Country.
firstNations.onCountryDesc: Our education and skills work is designed to be delivered on Country, with Traditional Owners and community organisations, rather than only at the campus gate. The campus is a hub. The programme extends outward.
firstNations.onCountry1: Entry pathways into screen, broadcast, and virtual production, with mentoring and paid placements.
firstNations.onCountry3: Long-horizon capability building into durable, high-skill roles.
firstNations.onCountry4: Procurement pathways for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander owned businesses across construction, operations, and creative supply.
firstNations.creativeHeading: Country, at production scale. Audiences, on terms communities control.
firstNations.creativeDesc: Virtual production and LED volumes make it possible to render Country at production scale without disturbing it. Live broadcast, AR, and VR open new paths to audiences. The campus is built to help First Nations storytellers reach national and international audiences on terms they control.
firstNations.evidence1: Board and executive governance arrangements, including the COO’s portfolio and decision rights.
firstNations.evidence2: IP and data provenance framework, including protocols for First Nations material.
firstNations.evidence3: Targets and reporting commitments for employment, procurement, and training.
firstNations.evidence4: Partnership and community relationships through which the programme is delivered.
firstNations.evidence5: Alignment with relevant NSW Government policy, including the Aboriginal Procurement Policy and Closing the Gap commitments.

meta.title: Network — Production City
meta.description: A sequenced global network of vertically integrated studio campuses. Sydney first. Switzerland, Singapore, Africa, and the United States follow. One operator. One origin.

network.heading: One origin. Sequenced expansion.
network.lead: Sydney is first. Switzerland is leading in Europe. Singapore is preferred in the Asia-Pacific. Africa is under assessment. United States sites follow.
network.sydneyDesc: First campus. Technical standards, R&D, and executive functions based here. In active development.
network.switzerlandDesc: Currently leading candidate for the European campus. Assessment ongoing.
network.singaporeDesc: Preferred candidate for the Asia-Pacific campus. Assessment in progress.
network.usaDesc: US sites committed once first international campuses are established.
network.sequenceDesc: The first campus is built, tuned, and operating before the next is committed. Errors in design, operations, or culture are caught at the first site, not replicated across a network.
network.operatorDesc: Each campus operates under the same brand, the same technology stack, and the same ownership model. Tenants and partners deal with one entity regardless of which campus they are on.

meta.title: The company — Production City
meta.description: Production City is an Australian company that designs, builds, and operates vertically integrated content production campuses. Sydney is the first site, not a branch.

company.heading: A first site, not a branch.
company.lead: Production City is an Australian company that designs, builds, and operates vertically integrated content production campuses. Sydney is the first of them. Switzerland, Singapore, Africa, and the United States follow.
company.what1: Production City combines established production craft with modern technology inside a single vertically integrated campus. The technology stack includes virtual production, LED volumes, motion capture, AR and VR, and connected broadcast — all designed together, not retrofitted.
company.what2: We operate the venue, the technology, and the services ourselves, under one brand. That reduces coordination risk for tenants and opens multiple revenue streams for the company.
company.what3: Our international footprint is being sequenced rather than launched simultaneously. Sydney leads. Switzerland is currently leading in Europe. Singapore is preferred in Asia-Pacific. Africa is under assessment. United States sites follow once the first international campuses are established.
company.pillar1Desc: One operator. One campus. Venue, technology stack, and full creative services — from script to delivery — under one brand.
company.pillar2Title: A First Nations approach, embedded throughout
company.pillar2Desc: Governance, intellectual property and data practice, workforce, and the stories this campus is built to serve — shaped by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of Knowing, Being, and Doing.
company.pillar3Desc: Broadcast and data-centre pedigree informs how the company engineers. Uptime, safety, and operational reliability come from that discipline.
company.pillar4Desc: Sydney first, then Switzerland, Singapore, Africa, United States. One site built, tuned and operating before the next is committed.
company.pillar5Desc: Sustainable design principles, energy and waste performance, biodiversity on the campus plan, and community dialogue that is ongoing rather than commissioning-phase.
company.leadershipNote: The wider executive team brings senior experience in screen education, animation and visual effects, virtual production and broadcast technology, music rights and US partnerships, and industry engagement. Full bios for each executive and non-executive director are provided on request.
company.partnersIntro: Production City is in advanced engagement across four partner categories. Named partners and the nature of each arrangement are disclosed where commercial confidentiality allows.
company.partner1Desc: Tertiary and training partners to establish a talent pipeline and skills development programme from campus opening. Specific pathways are co-designed with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education providers and community organisations.
company.partner2Desc: Major providers in virtual production, LED volume, real-time rendering, broadcast, and connected production. The technology stack is set at the first site and replicated across the network.
company.partner3Desc: Capital and research partners co-investing in innovation capability embedded in the campus, rather than adjacent to it. Research is treated as infrastructure, not overhead.
company.partner4Desc: First Nations owned businesses, community organisations, and Traditional Owner groups whose involvement shapes the workforce, procurement, cultural safety, and creative work of the campus.
company.partnersNote: Named partners are disclosed where commercial confidentiality allows. Early-stage engagements remain under commercial terms until agreements are signed.
company.pullQuote: The first campus is being built now. Technical standards, research and development, and the executive functions of the network are based at that first site. Being first is not a branding claim — it is a structural one, and it compounds.

meta.title: Approach — Production City
meta.description: The operating model, in one page.

companyApproach.heading: Built together. Not retrofitted.
companyApproach.lead: The operating model, in one page.
companyApproach.vert1: The traditional studio model coordinates many vendors across many sites. That works, but it moves the risk and the cost onto the production.
companyApproach.vert2: Production City operates the venue, the technology, and the full creative service stack ourselves, under one brand. Coordination risk sits with us. Revenue streams are diversified across facilities, services, and broadcast — which is part of why this model is bankable at the scale of a campus.
companyApproach.vert3: This is also why we can make commitments to tenants about pipeline time. A set built in our workshop does not leave the campus to reach the stage. A take finished in the gallery is graded a floor away. A live performance is broadcast from the control room without a second production being stood up around it.
companyApproach.vert4: The argument is simple. The execution is not. The team that engineered the campus came to it from broadcast, from data-centre infrastructure, and from production craft — which is closer to the actual demand than a pure property development approach.
companyApproach.platformDesc: A complex production and site management system is in design. It will handle scheduling, crew, tenants, billing, and broadcast orchestration at campus scale. That system is operator-facing, not public. This website will link to tenant and partner portals when they exist.
